title: The Cold War ‘red telephone’ was never a telephone
body: After the 1962 Cuban Missile Crisis exposed how slowly messages moved between the superpowers, the US and the Soviet Union opened a direct link in 1963. It carried text only, on teleprinters, because speech might be misinterpreted. It moved to fax in 1986 and to a secure computer link in 2008. The first test message was a pangram: ‘THE QUICK BROWN FOX JUMPED OVER THE LAZY DOG’S BACK 1234567890’.

slides.heading: The hotline’s technology over the years
slides.note: Text at every stage: no voice line, and no red telephone.

slides.question: Why did the 1963 hotline carry text rather than voice?
options: Phone lines could not reach Moscow
Voice calls were easier to tap
slides.explanation: It used teleprinters because spoken words might be misinterpreted. The link moved to fax in 1986 and to a secure computer link in 2008.

slides.heading: Fact or myth?

items.text: It was a red telephone on the president’s desk
Its first messages were typed on teleprinters
Leaders could speak to each other by voice over it
The US end was in the Pentagon, not the White House

slides.explanation: The link has never carried voice: teleprinters, then fax, then a secure computer link. Its US terminal is in the Pentagon’s National Military Command Center.
